title: Russell 1000 Versus Russell 2000 (R2000-R1000)
label: Russell 2000 Vs Russell 1000

narrative.compAhead: Small caps leading often goes with risk appetite and expectations of stronger domestic growth or easier financing.
narrative.baseAhead: A large-cap lead often goes with risk-averse positioning, tighter financing conditions or expectations of slower growth.

title: Russell 1000 Versus Russell Mid Cap (RMID-R1000)
label: Russell Mid Cap Vs Russell 1000

narrative.compAhead: Mid caps leading can point to broadening participation beyond the largest companies and confidence in the economic cycle.
narrative.baseAhead: Large caps leading points to concentration in the biggest, most established companies, often in uncertain or late-cycle markets.
narrative.note: Mid Cap via the IWR ETF

title: Russell 2000 Versus Russell Mid Cap (R2000-RMID)
label: Russell 2000 Vs Russell Mid Cap

narrative.compAhead: Small caps beating mid caps suggests investors are reaching further down the size spectrum for risk.
narrative.baseAhead: Mid caps beating small caps suggests a preference for more established, profitable companies over the smallest and most leveraged.
narrative.note: Mid Cap via the IWR ETF

title: Russell 1000 Value Versus Russell 1000 Growth (R1VAL-R1GRO)
label: Russell 1000 Value Vs Russell 1000 Growth

narrative.compAhead: Value leading often goes with rising yields, a cyclical recovery, or rotation out of expensive growth names.
narrative.baseAhead: Growth leading often goes with falling yields, scarce earnings growth or enthusiasm for a few large secular winners.
narrative.note: via the IWD and IWF ETFs

title: Russell 2000 Value Versus Russell 2000 Growth (R2VAL-R2GRO)
label: Russell 2000 Value Vs Russell 2000 Growth

narrative.compAhead: Small-cap value leading often goes with an early-cycle recovery and improving credit conditions.
narrative.baseAhead: Small-cap growth leading often goes with speculative risk appetite or lower rates, since many of these companies are not yet profitable.
narrative.note: via the VTWV and VTWG ETFs

title: S&P 500 Versus the NASDAQ Composite (NASD-SP500)
label: S&P 500 Vs Nasdaq Composite

narrative.compAhead: The Nasdaq leading points to strength in technology and high-growth names, often alongside risk-on sentiment.
narrative.baseAhead: The S&P 500 leading points to a broader market with less reliance on technology, often as investors rotate into other sectors.

title: S&P 500 Versus S&P 500 Quality (SPQUAL-SP500)
label: S&P 500 Vs S&P 500 Quality

narrative.compAhead: Quality leading suggests investors are paying up for strong balance sheets and steady earnings, often a defensive signal.
narrative.baseAhead: The broad index leading suggests lower-quality or more cyclical names are doing the lifting, often in risk-on phases.

title: US Total Market Versus US Consumer Discretionary (USCD-USTOT)
label: US Consumer Discretionary Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Consumer discretionary leading points to confidence in consumer spending and the economic cycle.
narrative.baseAhead: Consumer discretionary lagging can reflect concern about household spending, interest rates or the cycle.
narrative.note: via the IYC and ITOT ETFs

title: US Total Market Versus US Consumer Staples (USCS-USTOT)
label: US Consumer Staples Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Staples leading is usually defensive: investors favoring steady, recession-resistant earnings.
narrative.baseAhead: Staples lagging usually reflects risk appetite, with money moving to more cyclical areas.
narrative.note: via the IYK and ITOT ETFs

title: US Total Market Versus US Health Care (USHC-USTOT)
label: US Health Care Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Health care leading is often a defensive signal, or reflects sector news such as drug approvals or policy.
narrative.baseAhead: Health care lagging often reflects risk-on rotation, or sector pressure such as drug-pricing policy.
narrative.note: via the IYH and ITOT ETFs

title: US Total Market Versus US Financials (USFIN-USTOT)
label: US Financials Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Financials leading often goes with a steeper yield curve, healthy credit and expectations of economic growth.
narrative.baseAhead: Financials lagging can reflect a flat or inverted yield curve, credit worries or slowing loan growth.
narrative.note: via the IYF and ITOT ETFs

title: US Total Market Versus US Basic Materials (USMAT-USTOT)
label: US Materials Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Materials leading often goes with rising commodity prices, global industrial demand or inflation concerns.
narrative.baseAhead: Materials lagging often reflects soft commodity prices or weaker global industrial demand.
narrative.note: via the IYM and ITOT ETFs

title: US Total Market Versus US Industrials (USIND-USTOT)
label: US Industrials Vs US Total Market

narrative.compAhead: Industrials leading points to confidence in capital spending and the economic cycle.
narrative.baseAhead: Industrials lagging can signal concern about capital spending, trade or the economic cycle.
narrative.note: via the IYJ and ITOT ETFs

title: S&P 500 Versus the S&P/TSX Composite (TSX-SP500)
label: S&P 500 Vs TSX Composite

narrative.compAhead: Canada leading often goes with strong commodity and bank performance, since energy, materials and financials make up a large share of the TSX.
narrative.baseAhead: The US leading often reflects the S&P 500's heavier technology weight and stronger growth expectations.

title: S&P/TSX Composite Versus the S&P/TSX Small Cap Index (TSXSCI-TSX)
label: TSX Small Cap Vs TSX Composite

narrative.compAhead: Canadian small caps leading often goes with rising commodity prices and risk appetite, since the small-cap index is heavy in resources.
narrative.baseAhead: The Composite leading points to a preference for large banks, pipelines and other established companies.
narrative.note: Small Cap via the XCS ETF

title: S&P/TSX Composite Versus the S&P/TSX Mining Index (TSXMIN-TSX)
label: TSX Mining Vs TSX Composite

narrative.compAhead: Miners leading usually tracks rising gold and base-metal prices, and often global growth or inflation worries.
narrative.baseAhead: Miners lagging usually reflects falling metal prices or a firm US dollar.

title: S&P/TSX Composite Versus the S&P/TSX Banking Index (TSXBANKS-TSX)
label: TSX Banks Vs TSX Composite

narrative.compAhead: Banks leading often goes with a healthy credit cycle and steady housing and lending activity.
narrative.baseAhead: Banks lagging can reflect concern about credit losses, housing or a flat yield curve.

title: MSCI ACWI Versus MSCI ACWI Ex US Stocks (ACWIEXUS-ACWI)
label: MSCI ACWI Vs MSCI ACWI Ex US

narrative.compAhead: Non-US stocks leading means the rest of the world is beating the US, often alongside a weaker US dollar and broader global growth.
narrative.baseAhead: Global stocks beating non-US stocks means the US is leading, often on a strong dollar and US technology.
narrative.note: via the ACWX and ACWI ETFs

title: MSCI EAFE Versus the MSCI EAFE Small Cap Index (EAFESC-EAFE)
label: EAFE Small Cap Vs EAFE

narrative.compAhead: International small caps leading often signals confidence in the domestic economies of Europe and Japan.
narrative.baseAhead: International large caps leading points to a preference for global multinationals over domestically exposed companies.
narrative.note: via the SCZ and EFA ETFs

title: MSCI EAFE Value Versus the MSCI EAFE Growth Index (EAFEV-EAFEG)
label: EAFE Value Vs EAFE Growth

narrative.compAhead: International value leading often goes with rising rates and strength in banks and energy, which are heavy in the value index.
narrative.baseAhead: International growth leading often goes with falling rates and a preference for steady compounders.
narrative.note: via the EFV and EFG ETFs
